blocks.text: Neoclassical Pomo is an architectural design prominent between late 1970s to 1990s that mixes classical Roman and Greek architectural elements such as pediments, columns, and symmetry with the ironic, playful, and eclectic spirit of Postmodernism.
Post-modern Irony: Utilizes historical shapes in whimsical, unconventional, or fragmented ways rather than strict historical accuracy.
Interior Design: Dramatic lobbies featuring stylized columns and faux-ruin elements next to modern furniture.
Architecture Style: Corporate office civic centers, complexes, and post-modern public plazas.
Material Mix: Diffuses traditional marble and stone looks with neon, glass, synthetic finishes, and bright pastels.
Classical Elements: Features exaggerated arches, columns, symmetrical, and obelisks facades.
Graphic and Digital Art: Early vaporwave-adjacent aesthetics and computer-generated graphics featuring floating digital columns, and classical statues.
